s: Before approving a migration, a company's CIO asks for a data-driven business case that compares the current on-premises cost of 1,200 Windows Server and SQL Server VMs with the projected cost on AWS. The comparison must include right-sized instance recommendations and Microsoft licensing options (bring your own license and license included). Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST effort?
o: Request a Migration Evaluator assessment and use its Agentless Collector (or an inventory export) to collect utilization data. Use the resulting business case.
Enter each VM into the AWS Pricing Calculator manually, and compare the estimate with the on-premises costs in a spreadsheet.
Use AWS Compute Optimizer to produce right-sizing recommendations for the on-premises VMs.
Use AWS Cost Explorer forecasting to project the cost of running the VMs on AWS for the next 12 months.

w.y: Migration Evaluator is the no-cost AWS service for building a migration business case: it collects inventory and utilization (agentless collector or imported data), right-sizes, and compares on-premises TCO with AWS, including BYOL versus license-included options for Microsoft workloads. This matches the exam guide skill 'evaluating total cost of ownership (TCO)'.

o.A: Correct. It produces the TCO comparison, right-sizing and licensing analysis with little effort from the company.
o.B: The Pricing Calculator estimates AWS cost only; entering 1,200 VMs by hand is slow and it does not right-size from real utilization or model on-premises cost.
o.C: Compute Optimizer analyzes resources that already run on AWS. It cannot see on-premises VMs.
o.D: Cost Explorer forecasts existing AWS spend. It knows nothing about workloads not yet on AWS.
